caption: The drawing depicts the interior of a tobacco shop decorated in a vintage style with intricate details. At the top of the image, there are framed black-and-white portraits labeled "McKinley" and "Victoria," draped with black bunting. Two flags, one American (left) and one British (right), hang on either side of the portraits. The ceiling has a beige and light gray geometric pattern. Ornate brass chandeliers hang from the ceiling. Below, a wooden counter with a glass display case holds cigars and tobacco products, with an old-fashioned cash register on the left side and baskets of small items nearby. On the right wall, there are built-in wooden shelves filled with packages, boxes, and tins of various tobacco products; visible labels include “FIVE BROTHER CHEWING TOBACCO” and “BULL.” A carved wooden Indian figure in a feathered headdress stands behind a black metal railing near the back, surrounded by baskets. A pair of white animal statues, likely horses, are inside the railing area. The floor consists of alternating black-and-white hexagonal tiles. Advertisements and product signs, many with bright, multicolored designs, are positioned above the shelves on the right wall, one showing a Native American scene, another labeled "Good Luck." The overall color palette consists mainly of brown wood, green counters, white-and-black flooring, and assorted brighter colors from product packaging and signage.
title: Cigar Store, 1901
